answer: Neighborhood Beacon Test: each identity must emit a periodic beacon whose timing is checked against its declared neighbors' clocks. A cluster of accounts created together shows synchronized drift and a shared fable of independent history that fails the ripple test—real neighbors propagate timing jitter recursively. Enforcement: flags propagate transitively, so one caught cluster taints all accounts within k hops. Cost: an attacker must acquire and run genuinely desynchronized hosts per identity, paying isolation overhead per node.
